notes.text:
The Facebook friend graph never disappeared. It just became infrastructure — one of many inputs into the feed algorithm, consumed at the API layer, invisible to the actual user.

The same thing is starting to happen to the CRM.

Salesforce isn't going away. But the account executive who opens his laptop and finds a research agent, a dialer coach, and an orchestration layer waiting for him — that stack is the newsfeed. That's where the valuable thing lives now.
notes.source: The post's central analogy: the Facebook friend graph becoming an API-layer input to the news feed, mapped onto CRM becoming just one input into the system of intelligence.

notes.text:
CRM usage has actually gone up since AI agents started taking over GTM workflows.

Not down. Up.

The agents listening to calls and writing structured notes back in are making the underlying data richer than it's ever been — giving reps fresh reason to consult a system they used to neglect.

But here's the tension: the more AI agents automate the workflows on top, the more the CRM looks like a database rather than a destination. A very large, carefully curated, well-integrated database. But a database nonetheless.
notes.source: The counterintuitive finding from the GTM survey that CRM usage has risen since AI adoption, paired with the argument that the CRM is becoming infrastructure.

notes.text:
A VP of Sales, a few years from now, doesn't start her morning in Salesforce staring at a static account list.

She opens a prioritized feed: which accounts had material news overnight, which prospects just came in-market, which pipeline deals have gone suspiciously quiet.

Her new hire six weeks in is walking into meetings better prepped than the ten-year veteran at the next desk.

And when a rep leaves, the institutional memory — every account nuance, every relationship built over years — doesn't walk out with them.

This is what it looks like when the system of intelligence becomes the product.
notes.source: The post's 'VP of Sales a few years hence' scene describing the daily prioritization feed, better-prepared reps, and institutional memory as a shippable asset.
